pull_request.title: Permission refactor, verify `cursor_mut_at` and `PageTablePageMeta::on_drop`
pull_request.body:
This PR verifies `PageTablePageMeta::on_drop` and `cursor_mut_at`. Required the change I mentioned in PR 454, removing the locally carried, typed slot perms from owner objects and instead keeping them in a `MetaRegionOwners` object at all times. This was a big change, but a good one; the old model made sense when we didn't have good &mut support, but now we can borrow those permissions from `MetaRegionOwners` instead, via `borrow_typed_perm` and `borrow_mut_typed_perm` axioms. This lets us eliminate the excess preconditions on `cursor_mut_at`. It also removes some of the complexity in `on_drop`, where we previously had to collect the permissions for the dropped children separately instead of assuming that they were in `regions`.

I've also simplified the `Guards` structure to carry the set of addresses with corresponding guards. It still carries a lifetime, and the places where we used `'static` are fixed. It no longer needs a `PageTableConfig` parameter, meaning that we don't need separate `Guards` structures for kernel and userspace.

nodes.bodyHTML:
Pull request overview

This PR refactors the page-table/meta-slot permission model to keep typed slot permissions parked in MetaRegionOwners and to simplify guard tracking, in order to relax cursor preconditions and simplify/verify PageTablePageMeta::on_drop.

Changes:

  • Added metadata-only borrow/write support (Meta(...)) to the borrow_field! / update_field! helper macros.
  • Strengthened/adjusted ReprPtr/PointsTo postconditions to track inner_perms more explicitly.
  • Removed PageTableConfig from Guards and rewired VmSpace, cursors, and page-table node code to use Guards<'rcu> plus the centralized MetaRegionOwners permission parking model.
  • Refactored PageTablePageMeta::on_drop to rely on regions.slots (instead of locally-carried child perms) and updated its signature to accept regions + vm_io_owner directly.

Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 34 out of 35 changed files in this pull request and generated 8 comments.

File Description
vstd_extra/src/trans_macros.rs Adds Meta(...) macro arms to enable metadata-only reads/writes through Metadata::{borrow_meta, borrow_meta_mut}.
vstd_extra/src/cast_ptr.rs Tightens specifications around inner_perms preservation/updates for take/put, and strengthens PointsTo::new with an explicit postcondition.
ostd/src/mm/vm_space.rs Switches VmSpace construction and cursor APIs to use the simplified Guards<'rcu> (no PageTableConfig parameter).
ostd/src/mm/page_table/node/mod.rs Updates PageTablePageMeta::on_drop to the new regions-owned permission model and rewires node allocation/locking specs to the new Guards<'rcu> shape.

💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

review_comments.body: These newly introduced `exec fn`s have `unimplemented!()` bodies. They are called from runtime code paths (e.g., `MetaSlot::write_meta` calls `Metadata::<M>::write_metadata_into_storage`), so this will panic at runtime as soon as a frame is initialized. Provide a real implementation (likely via an unsafe write into the `PCell<MetaSlotStorage>` plus the appropriate spec guarantees), or gate the call sites so this code is never executed in non-verification builds.

The new `borrow_field!(..., Meta(...))` macro arm calls this in executable code (e.g., linked-list operations), so it would panic at runtime. This needs a real implementation that returns a shared `&M` backed by the slot storage while respecting the permission model.

+    /// Read-only mirror of [`borrow_meta_mut`]: yields a shared `&M` into the
+    /// storage cell, with no perm-roundtrip noise. Lifetime is tied to the
+    /// shared `&` perm borrow.
+    #[verifier::external_body]
+    pub exec fn borrow_meta<'a>(
+        slot_ptr: cast_ptr::ReprPtr<MetaSlot, Metadata<M>>,
+        Tracked(perm): Tracked<&'a cast_ptr::PointsTo<MetaSlot, Metadata<M>>>,
+    ) -> (res: &'a M)
+        requires
+            perm.pptr() == slot_ptr,
+            perm.is_init(),
+            perm.wf(&perm.inner_perms),
+        ensures
+            *res == perm.value().metadata,
+    {
+        unimplemented!()
+    }
+
+    /// Borrow only the inner `M` (the `metadata` field) mutably from a typed
+    /// slot cast_ptr perm. Touches only the underlying storage cell:
+    /// `ref_count`/`in_list`/`vtable_ptr` perms and values are bit-identical
+    /// across the borrow, and the outer `points_to` value is preserved (cell
+    /// IDs and `vtable_ptr` address are unchanged, so the reconstructed
+    /// `MetaSlot` is structurally equal by `meta_slot_eq_by_ids`).
+    ///
+    /// This is a surgical alternative to `take`/`put` on `Metadata<M>` for
+    /// the common case of mutating one field of the in-cell `M`: callers
+    /// avoid the per-write `perm_u64_with_identity` / `pptr_usize_with_identity`
+    /// / `metadata_perms_inverse` triad they would need to discharge after a
+    /// full Repr roundtrip. The exec implementation is a one-cell unsafe
+    /// cast (the storage cell's value is already an `M`); the spec lives at
+    /// the same trust boundary as `metadata_from_inner_perms` /
+    /// `inner_perms_from_metadata`.
+    #[verifier::external_body]
+    pub exec fn borrow_meta_mut<'a>(
+        slot_ptr: cast_ptr::ReprPtr<MetaSlot, Metadata<M>>,
+        Tracked(perm): Tracked<&'a mut cast_ptr::PointsTo<MetaSlot, Metadata<M>>>,
+    ) -> (res: &'a mut M)
+        requires
+            old(perm).pptr() == slot_ptr,
+            old(perm).is_init(),
+            old(perm).wf(&old(perm).inner_perms),
+        ensures
+    // Initial: the lent `M` is the current value's `metadata`.
+
+            *res == old(perm).value().metadata,
+            // Outer perm shape preserved.
+            final(perm).pptr() == old(perm).pptr(),
+            final(perm).is_init(),
+            final(perm).wf(&final(perm).inner_perms),
+            // Value: only `metadata` may change.
+            final(perm).value() == (Metadata {
+                metadata: *final(res),
+                ref_count: old(perm).value().ref_count,
+                vtable_ptr: old(perm).value().vtable_ptr,
+                in_list: old(perm).value().in_list,
+            }),
+            // Outer points_to value is bit-identical (all cell IDs preserved,
+            // and `vtable_ptr` address preserved, so by `meta_slot_eq_by_ids`
+            // the reconstructed `MetaSlot` equals the old one).
+            final(perm).points_to == old(perm).points_to,
+            // Accessory inner perms are untouched.
+            final(perm).inner_perms.ref_count == old(perm).inner_perms.ref_count,
+            final(perm).inner_perms.in_list == old(perm).inner_perms.in_list,
+            final(perm).inner_perms.vtable_ptr == old(perm).inner_perms.vtable_ptr,
+            // Storage cell is re-encoded for the final `M`.
+            final(perm).inner_perms.storage == Self::inner_perms_from_metadata(
+                *final(res),
+                old(perm).inner_perms.storage,
+            ),
+    {
+        unimplemented!()
+    }
review_comments.body: `Metadata::borrow_meta_mut` is an `exec fn` but still `unimplemented!()`. `update_field!(..., Meta(...))` depends on this to mutate metadata fields in place; leaving it unimplemented will panic at runtime and defeats the purpose of the refactor. Implement this (likely via an unsafe `&mut` borrow of the metadata storage) or avoid calling it in executable code.

review_comments.body: `write_meta` currently writes `0` into `vtable_ptr`. Unless `vtable_ptr` is intentionally unused everywhere at runtime, this breaks dynamic metadata drop/dispatch (and even if unused today, it leaves an invalid value in memory). It should write the actual vtable pointer for `metadata as &dyn AnyFrameMeta` (or otherwise initialize `vtable_ptr` consistently with how `drop_meta_in_place` reconstructs the trait object).

review_comments.body: `Metadata::borrow_meta_mut` is an `exec fn` but still `unimplemented!()`. `update_field!(..., Meta(...))` depends on this to mutate metadata fields in place; leaving it unimplemented will panic at runtime and defeats the purpose of the refactor. Implement this (likely via an unsafe `&mut` borrow of the metadata storage) or avoid calling it in executable code.

review_comments.body: `write_meta` currently writes `0` into `vtable_ptr`. Unless `vtable_ptr` is intentionally unused everywhere at runtime, this breaks dynamic metadata drop/dispatch (and even if unused today, it leaves an invalid value in memory). It should write the actual vtable pointer for `metadata as &dyn AnyFrameMeta` (or otherwise initialize `vtable_ptr` consistently with how `drop_meta_in_place` reconstructs the trait object).
